column1: # EVERYTHING RAISED ONCE THE MODULE COMPILES, on the way from JDK 17 to JDK 21.
# Not polish, and it used to say it was. This carries the versions the test run needs as
# well as the ones the scanner does: mockito and byte-buddy so the suite can mock under the
# new class file major, archunit and jacoco so they stop rejecting it, jaxb and
# javax.annotation because JEP 320 took them out of the JDK. None of those is needed for a
# compile, which is why they wait until after one.
# Every row is the head of a line and answers only for projects already on it: same major, same
# minor, lower patch. One artifact may hold several rows, one per line.
# group:artifact <tab> version <tab> any|maven|gradle <tab> other spellings, comma separated
# WHY THESE TOMCAT VERSIONS. Measured on this corpus, not read off a compatibility table:
# tomcat-embed-core 9.0.65 scores 22 CRITICAL+HIGH, 9.0.83 scores 19, 9.0.105 scores 14. Nothing in
# a Java bump ever looked at that. Tomcat moved because SPRING moved -- Boot 2.7.18 pins
# tomcat.version 9.0.83 -- so a project inherited whichever Tomcat its framework happened to carry,
# and 9.0.83 is the last patch of Boot 2.7's line rather than of Tomcat's. 10.1.55 is what Boot
# 3.5.16 pins, and the exact version trivy names as the fix for what the newest Tomcat 9 carries.
# The family moves in lockstep or the build breaks: tomcat-embed-core, -el and -websocket share a
# WHY 3.5 AND NOT 2.7 ABOVE JDK 17. Spring Boot 2.7 does not support Java 21. It was the last 2.x
# line and went end of life in 2023, so a 17 to 21 hop that lifts a Boot 2.7.3 project to 2.7.18 has
# moved it to the newest patch of a line that cannot run the target. The measurement agrees: this
# corpus scores Boot 3.5.x at 1 CRITICAL+HIGH against 2.7.18's tens.
# The cost is honest and large. 2 to 3 is the jakarta rename, the highest-variance migration in this
# system, and the one measured losing 1916 of 2409 tests on a repository that took the jump
# unprepared. It is attempted anyway because the gate is the arbiter, and because leaving a project
# on an end-of-life line that cannot run its own target is not a smaller risk, only a quieter one.
# JACKSON-DATABIND, ONE ROW PER LINE, AND ONLY THE TOP TWO REACH ZERO.
# Measured across 153 traces, from packages-before as well as packages-after, so it covers versions
# no bump ever chose. Every line from 2.12 to 2.20 bottoms out at 2 CRITICAL+HIGH whatever patch it
# older patches on those lines. 2.21.4 scores 0 over 44 observations and 2.22.0 scores 0.
# So a patch is worth taking and is not a fix. It is worth taking because the alternative is worse:
# 2.13.0 scores 6 and 2.13.5 scores 2, 2.10.0 scores 7, 2.9.4 scores 62. It is not a fix because
# only a LINE move reaches zero, and a line move is not a pin.
# Every version here was checked to carry a real jar in the mirror rather than a directory a failed
# lookup left behind, which is why 2.12 ends at 2.12.7.1: 2.12.7.2 has a directory and no jar.
# The lines below 2.10 have no measurement at all, because nothing in this corpus ever resolved
# their heads. Those rows are a fact about the mirror and a guess about the benefit.
# EVERY LINE WHERE A PATCH DEMONSTRABLY CLEARS SOMETHING, mined rather than chosen.
# Read off packages-before and packages-after across 153 traces: for each artifact, each major.minor
# it was seen on, and the CRITICAL+HIGH each patch carried. A line earns a row here only where one
# patch measured strictly better than another on the SAME line, so every row is a fix somebody in
# this corpus has already been shown to need.
# The version is the latest patch that reaches the lowest measured count, and where that count is
# still above zero it is the newest patch the mirror carries instead, because a fix that landed
# after our last observation is more likely in the newer one. Every version was checked to have a
# real jar. Vendor rebuilds are excluded: atlassian, redhat, jboss and the rest carry their own
# version schemes and a floor written to one of them cannot be met by a project on upstream.
# MOST OF THESE ARE MANAGED ON A BOOT OR QUARKUS MODULE, and that does not make them wrong here. It
# makes them the definition of "still short after the platform raise", which is the only condition
# under which the platform fragments allow a member to be pinned directly.
